name: IN-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -15 partisan lean
Incumbent Erin Houchin running with a large financial advantage
Polymarket prices Houchin at roughly 92% to win
Democrat Brad Meyer has raised only about $105K with no outside spending
model.rationale: The district's -15 Republican lean, Houchin's incumbency and roughly $1.2 million war chest against Meyer's modest fundraising, and prediction markets pricing her near 92% all point to a comfortable Republican hold with little evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or polling showing Meyer within single digits would be the first sign this race is moving toward competitiveness.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southern Indiana's 9th District leans heavily Republican, and first-term incumbent Erin Houchin is seeking re-election with the advantages that typically come with the seat. She has raised about $1.9 million and holds more than $1.1 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Brad Meyer has raised roughly $105,000 and reports under $20,000 in the bank. No outside groups are active on either side, and no expert ratings or general-election polls are available for the race.

Prediction markets give Houchin about a 92% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. A Libertarian candidate is on the ballot but has raised almost nothing. Absent unexpected news or spending, this race is expected to remain firmly in Republican hands.
